recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No FHIR core source change is needed unless BR&R later chooses a substantive remodel of allergen status on SubstanceDefinition.
issue_request: FHIR-31814 was a Published/Persuasive BR&R change request for R5 saying Ingredient.allergenIndicator/allergenicIndicator describes a substance property, not an ingredient property, and asking that if the element remains available for coded substances it should have an invariant limiting use to that case. The accepted resolution was to add the invariant.
initial_application: The change was applied before this reconciliation in February 2022 Ingredient commits, especially 464b98e6e7, which added invariant ing-1 and expanded the Ingredient.allergenicIndicator definition. Earlier same-family commit 2e1674b1a6 carried the same application. Later commits a75aa13680c and 41d2b22c8d refined the FHIRPath and spelling without changing the rule.
additional_context: Ingredient is active in source/fhir.ini and SubstanceDefinition is active/approved and is the target profile for Ingredient.substance.code references. FHIR-31839 touched the same element's meaningWhenMissing in the same implementation family and is already represented on the combined branch, so it was not decided again. Community searches found no conflicting Zulip or Confluence decision.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. The current source has invariant ing-1 preventing allergenicIndicator=true with Ingredient.substance.code.reference, and the definition tells readers that allergen information belongs on SubstanceDefinition when a SubstanceDefinition reference is used.

related_jiras.note: Same historical Ingredient commit family updated meaningWhenMissing on Ingredient.allergenicIndicator; already audited on the combined branch.
Later spelling cleanup corrected the FHIR-31814 invariant and definition text without changing the accepted rule.
